key_insight: Topo-Spectral Percolation Descriptors (TSPD) can infer ion-transport mechanisms directly from a single static crystal structure by combining barrier-based migration networks with topological percolation analysis and graph spectral features.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, calibration-free screening of solid electrolytes and other ion-conducting materials to identify dimensionality, bottlenecks, and viable pathways before expensive molecular dynamics simulations.
method: Build a periodic migration network from the crystal structure.
Assign physics-based edge barriers and analyze barrier-threshold percolation.
Use the spectrum of the barrier-weighted graph Laplacian to classify transport pathways.
evidence_signal: The authors validate TSPD against AIMD ion densities and neutron diffraction data for eight materials spanning 1D to 3D transport, and it reproduces the established mechanism in every case.
watch_item: TSPD is most informative for pathway-limited, direction-dependent transport and may be less decisive for strongly cooperative or nearly isotropic ion motion.
paper_title: Topo-Spectral Percolation Descriptors for Mechanistic Ion Transport Pathways from Static Crystal Structures
